title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from pp. 109–112 of the manuscript: Grothendieck is formalising the combinatorics of a normal-crossings divisor at infinity. The intended application is the Deligne–Mumford boundary of M_{g,ν}.

Notation:
- D_d is the normalised locus where d local branches meet.
- D̃_d → D_d is the principal S_d-covering obtained by ordering the d branches.
- For a finite totally ordered 'flag type' J, D_J is the corresponding stratum datum. Its top element e_J has cardinal d.
- One has D_J ≃ D̃_d ∧^{S_d} H(J), where H(J) is a finite S_d-set: compatible choices h assigning to each x∈J a subset of I_d={1..d} of the right cardinal.
- For the two-step flag Δ(d,δ) (with δ<d), (155)/(160) give D_{d,δ} ≃ D̃_d ∧^{S_d} P_δ(I_d). Here P_δ(I_d) is the set of δ-element subsets of I_d. Geometrically, a point of D_{d,δ} is a point of the d-fold locus together with a choice of δ of its d branches.

On this page:
1. The evaluation map (161), h ↦ h(x), from H(J) to P_δ(I_d) (x∈J of cardinal δ) is S_d-equivariant.
2. Contracting with D̃_d therefore gives a morphism (162), f_x : D_J → D_{d,δ}. It is read through the vertical identifications D_J ≃ D̃_d∧H(J) and D_{d,δ} ≃ D̃_d∧P_δ(I_d). So this morphism is described purely in terms of the principal covering D̃_d and the combinatorics of J.
3. The functorial composite (158), D_J → D_{J'} → D_δ, is then extended to the commutative square (163). Its arrows D_J→D_{d,δ} and D_{d,δ}→D_δ are induced by functoriality from the inclusions {x}⊂{x,e}⊂J.
4. Conclusion, completed on the next page: every functoriality morphism D_J→D_{J'}, and the composites (158), is determined by the explicit maps (162) together with the 'boundary morphisms' D_{d,δ}→D_δ. The maps D_{d,δ}→D_d are the finite étale 'normal' morphisms of degree C(d,δ).

The next page goes on to the fibre-product rule D_{α,α'} ×_{D_{α'}} D_{α',α''} ≃ D_{α,α',α''}. In short, the page reduces the whole diagram of strata of a normal-crossings divisor to (i) the principal S_d-coverings D̃_d → D_d and (ii) the boundary maps D_{d,δ} → D_δ.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The arrow in (162) is a morphism, not an isomorphism; H(J)→P_δ(I_d) is in general neither injective nor surjective. The image reads 'd'où un morphisme', so the transcription's 'isomorphisme' is a misreading, not Grothendieck's error.

Minor gap: the claim that D_J → D_{d,δ} 'is described by' (162) inside the composite (158) is asserted without proof. It follows routinely from the functoriality of the contracted-product construction.
The (158) cross-reference is internally loose: (158) was written with d' while this page uses δ.

ideas.what: Describe the strata of a normal-crossings divisor as contracted products D̃_d ∧^{S_d} (finite S_d-set), using the principal S_d-covering given by ordering the local branches.
ideas.modern_name: Normalised strata of an snc/ncd divisor; branch-ordering S_d-torsor; finite étale covers via S_d-sets (Galois correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Deligne, Hodge II, 1971; Deligne–Mumford 1969 for the M_g boundary); systematised in log geometry (Kato, Illusie)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}

ideas.what: Functoriality maps between strata determined by 'boundary' morphisms D_{d,δ}→D_δ and finite étale 'normal' morphisms D_{d,δ}→D_d, indexed by flags of cardinals.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of strata over the poset/category of flags; boundary complex / dual complex of the divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (e.g. dual complexes: Danilov; modular operads and stable graphs for M_{g,n}: Getzler–Kapranov, Kontsevich–Manin)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine bookkeeping of the strata of a normal-crossings divisor via branch-ordering S_d-torsors and finite S_d-sets. It is standard material, and nothing here goes beyond what is known.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read 'compatible avec les opérations de S_d, d'où un morphisme', not 'isomorphisme'.

(162) layout: top row D_J --f_x--> D_{d,δ}. Below are vertical ≅ signs: D_J ≅ D̃_d ∧_{S_d} H(J) and D_{d,δ} ≅ D̃_d ∧_{S_d} P_δ(I_d). The 'D_d^!' is D̃_d with a tilde, and P_δ(I_d) is the set of δ-subsets.
The added phrase is likely 'et de x∈J', and the inserted note reads roughly 'On a un J de D_J'.
In (163) the inclusions are {x}⊂{x,e}⊂J, with e = e_J, not 'c'.
Next page: D_γ→D_γ' should be D_J→D_J', and 'compactés (158)' should be 'composés (158)'.
